messages:
Priya: quick sync — proposing a new runtime endpoint /v2/configs/apply?mode=staged that supports 'brushfire' propagation. basic idea:
Priya: - stage groups are weight-based but with rollback hooks
Priya: here's the proto I'm thinking:
```json
{ "stages": [ { "name": "initial", "pct": 1 }, { "name": "ramp", "pct": 50 } ], "rollback": { "on_error": "auto", "metrics": [ "p99_latency", "error_rate" ] } }
```
Jordan: hmm do we really want to pair propagation with automatic metric checks? what about noisy metric flapping?
Sam: +1 to metric gating but we need hysteresis and min-sample-size. also return a "preview diff" API so console can show expected route changes.
Ava: UI question — can we show per-stage estimated QPS and expected token cost? ops people need that.
Priya: yes — plan is the preview endpoint returns per-route projected qps and cost using recent 1h traffic model.
Jordan: implementation concern: runtime needs deterministic shard mapping when increasing pct to avoid cache churn. we should define "sticky cohorts" vs random.
Sam: sticky cohorts = consistent hashing on user_id, but what about anonymous traffic? session_id? any fallback?
Ava: for console, we can surface "cohort type" dropdown: user_id / session_id / request_hash; defaults to request_hash.
Priya: @ops-bot can we run a canary tomorrow on staging with these flags?
ops-bot: scheduled canary: staging-config-brushfire-6487654321 at 2026-03-22T02:00Z, 1h window. will report p99_latency and error_rate.
Jordan: also need an API error model: if preview and apply are inconsistent (race), apply should fail-fast with conflict code + human-readable diff.
Sam: agree. and add "safety_score" field to preview, computed from sample size, metric variance, and route-sensitivity.
Ava: UX nit: label the rollout with owner + runbook link. add a rollback button from console.
Priya: ack. I'll sketch the API contract and runbook tonight, pinging runtime team for shard behavior.
Jordan: re: quotas — staged increases must be capped by quota headroom. add a "quota_reserve" field in preview.
Priya: good call. final Q: anyone strongly against automatic rollback on metric breach? I'm leaning yes if metrics are high-confidence.
Sam: lean yes with a "dry-run" toggle that exercises detection without triggering rollback.
Ava: :thumbsup:
Priya: thanks all — I'll upload a PR with proto + open an RFC.
